verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2017 (Q9) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question text itself is sourced from that paper. `appearances` is deliberately left empty — a separate reviewed tagging pass fills it, and a hand-written tag here would be an invented claim. Physics hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13: the mean free path is the average distance travelled between two successive collisions, λ = 1/(√2 π d² n), with d the molecular diameter and n the number of molecules per unit volume; the √2 comes from the relative motion of the other molecules.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The definition
lines: The mean free path is the average
distance a molecule travels between two

lines.text: λ = total path length / number of collisions

steps.margin_note: First mark. The word average and the words successive collisions both carry it.
steps.why: A molecule does not travel far in a straight line. It moves freely, hits another molecule, changes direction and moves freely again. The free paths have different lengths, so the quantity that is useful is their average.
common_mistakes: Saying it is the distance between two molecules. It is the distance TRAVELLED between two collisions.

recall.must_convey: That mean free path is the average distance a molecule travels between two successive collisions.
reject: one by root two pi d squared n

steps.memory_tip: A free path is one run between two hits. Mean is the average of all those runs.

lines: d is the diameter of a molecule and n is
the number of molecules per unit volume.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name d and n after the formula; the symbols alone are not the mark.
steps.why: Both d and n sit in the denominator, so a denser gas or a larger molecule gives a shorter free path. The √2 is there because the other molecules are moving as well, not standing still.
common_mistakes: Reading n as the total number of molecules. n is the number per unit volume.
Dropping the √2 and writing λ = 1/(π d² n).

recall.must_convey: That lambda equals one by root two pi d squared n, with d the molecular diameter and n the number per unit volume.
accept: one by root two pi d squared n
n is the number per unit volume
heard_as: root two pi d squared n

steps.memory_tip: Larger molecules and more of them both shorten the run: d and n are both downstairs.

insider_note: The definition alone is one mark of two — add λ = 1/(√2 π d² n) with d and n named to take the second.
